analyst.summary: Tata Power's -4.7% FY26 revenue decline is confirmed in our PIT data and is real but substantially explained by a resolved one-off (Mundra UMPP's Q4FY26 PPA-expiry shutdown, fixed via a new supplemental PPA from April 2026) plus a coal-price pass-through optic, not core demand destruction -- consolidated PAT still hit an all-time high of Rs 5,118 cr (+7% YoY) on the back of a genuine Odisha-discom turnaround (first-ever dividends, AT&C losses down 15 points) and doubling regulated Mumbai transmission capex at a fixed 15.5% return. Against that, leverage is elevated and rising fast (non-current debt +40% YoY), FY27 capex guidance was already cut once on execution delays, and this review surfaced a live, UNPROVISIONED ~USD 490mn (~Rs 4,100 cr) SIAC arbitration award under an active arbitrator-impartiality controversy plus a second smaller unresolved Adaro arbitration -- risks the quant snapshot's single redflag tag understates. At ~32x trailing earnings for an 11.5%-ROCE utility-conglomerate with thin (1.4x-2.5x depending on basis) and worsening interest cover, the multiple prices in flawless execution of management's FY30 doubling ambition across renewables, manufacturing utilization, T&D capex and a Mundra plant with a decade-long history of PPA surprises. This is a genuine judgment call, but the added leverage trajectory and unpriced arbitration tail risk tip it to Sell for the existing holding.
